ABOUT US  
 
Fetch Personnel are an Australian owned recruitment company with 10 years’ experience specialising in Contract and Labour Hire across Commercial, Industrial and Residential Construction, plus major Civil Infrastructure Projects throughout Australia. 
 
 THE OPPORTUNITY  
 
Due to internal promotions and high client demand we are looking to add  2 Consultants  to our established  Labour Hire  team, which has grown to become one of the leading divisions here at Fetch. 
 
Demonstrated minimum of two years recruitment experience and/or equivalent qualifications are required as you will be managing a  Warm/Live  360 desk within either the  Construction  or  Civil Infrastructure  industry. 
 
We are a proven industry leader in our chosen fields, with have a large database of candidates, clients, with live jobs to work on from day 1. 
 
Key responsibilities include but not limited to: 

 
	 Manage recruitment process from start to finish for both Client and Candidate. 
	 Utilising various candidate sourcing strategies to successfully attract applicants. 
	 Qualify candidate suitability and client commitment for current or future vacancies. 
	 Maintain and develop current client relationships 
 

  
We are looking for people who are career driven, resilient and have good business acumen. A natural engaging approach, strong written and verbal communication skills are a must. If you are looking to drive your own business but want the support to achieve this, then this is the opportunity you have been waiting for. 
 
 OUR CULTURE:  
 
Fetch are proud to have one of the best staff retention rates within the Recruitment industry. 
 
Everyone is treated with respect and given autonomy to run their own desk, alongside experienced management who provide hands on mentoring plus assist with long standing relationships to help you achieve success 
 
We love to celebrate success and have a huge focus on our culture: 

 
	 Work alongside Industry leaders within the Construction, Engineering, Infrastructure and Labour Hire recruitment

	 26 days annual leave 
	 High achievers club 
	 Team building & Awards every quarter 
	 Networking functions 
	 Yearly team trips away 
	 End of month drinks 
	 New office complete with a barista style coffee machine, a table tennis table and library. 
 

  
Interested? Please apply below or call Dan Musto on 0455 337 866 for a confidential discussion.

result.description: Metalwork WA Pty Ltd   Position Overview   Metalwork WA Pty Ltd is seeking a skilled and motivated Full-time Metal Fabricator to join its fabrication team in Western Australia. The successful applicant will fabricate, assemble, install, maintain, modify, and repair structural steel and other fabricated metal products by interpreting engineering drawings, preparing metal materials, and carrying out welding and fabrication activities while maintaining high standards of quality, precision, and workplace safety.    Key Responsibilities    Interpret engineering drawings, blueprints, specifications, and work instructions.  Mark out, measure, cut, shape, and prepare metal sections, plates, pipes, and structural components.  Fabricate, assemble, and install structural steel, frames, platforms, handrails, brackets, truck bodies, and other fabricated metal products.  Fit, align, and join fabricated metal components using appropriate welding processes and fabrication techniques in accordance with engineering specifications.   Operate fabrication equipment including guillotines, press brakes, rollers, drills, saws, grinders, and other workshop machinery.  Inspect fabricated products to ensure dimensional accuracy and compliance with quality standards and engineering specifications.  Repair, modify, and maintain metal structures and fabricated products as required.  Maintain a safe, clean, and organised work environment while complying with workplace health and safety policies and procedures.  Maintain fabrication equipment and tools in a safe operating condition and comply with workplace health and safety procedures throughout all fabrication activities.     Skills and Experience   The successful applicant should possess:   A qualification relevant to metal fabrication, engineering fabrication, boilermaking, welding, or a closely related trade equivalent to AQF Certificate III including at least two years of on-the-job training, or AQF Certificate IV (ANZSCO Skill Level 3).  Demonstrated ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, fabrication plans, and technical specifications.  Experience in fabricating, assembling, fitting, installing, modifying, and repairing structural steel and fabricated metal products.   Competency in welding and the safe operation of fabrication machinery and associated hand and power tools.  Strong knowledge of metalworking techniques, measuring equipment, quality control processes, and workplace health and safety requirements.  Good communication skills, attention to detail, problem-solving ability, and the capacity to work effectively both independently and as part of a team.    What We Offer    Full-time permanent employment with an established Western Australian steel fabrication company.  Competitive remuneration commensurate with skills and experience.  Opportunity to work on diverse commercial, industrial, mining, and infrastructure fabrication projects.  A professional and safety-focused workplace with modern fabrication equipment.  Ongoing opportunities to develop technical skills and contribute to high-quality fabrication projects.  Supportive team environment with a commitment to quality workmanship and continuous improvement.    Application Process   Applicants must submit a resume and a cover letter outlining relevant experience and suitability for the role.  Metalwork WA Pty Ltd is an equal opportunity employer and supports a diverse workforce.  About Company     METALWORK WA PTY LTD  is a Western Australian steel fabrication company specialising in truck body building, structural steel, and architectural steel fabrication. The company provides end-to-end fabrication services, including design, drafting, manufacturing, blasting, painting, and on-site installation for commercial, industrial, construction, and mining clients. Operating from a fully equipped workshop in Perth, Metalwork WA delivers custom metal fabrication solutions, site welding, and steel construction projects while maintaining a strong commitment to quality, workplace safety, and timely project delivery. The company has been actively operating in Australia since 2009 as a registered Australian proprietary company.  Australian working rights

Position: Corporate Services Manager
Type: Full-time
Employer: Exaudy Care Pty Ltd
Location: Narre Warren VIC 3805
Salary: $87,000 p/a
About the Business:
Exaudy Care Pty Ltd is a registered NDIS provider based in Melbourne’s south-east, delivering high-quality, person-centred disability support services to participants with complex health, behavioural, and psychosocial needs across Victoria. Specialising in Support Coordination, Plan Management, Behaviour Support, Home and Living (SIL), Day Centre programs, Registered Nurse services, and community access, the organisation is committed to empowering individuals through tailored, goal-focused support that promotes independence, choice, and inclusion. Guided by its core values of Empathy, eXcellence, Accessibility, Understanding, Dedication, and You-focused care (“EXAUDY”), Exaudy Care fosters a compassionate, professional workplace culture where collaboration, continuous improvement, and regulatory excellence drive meaningful outcomes for participants, families, and the broader community.
About the Position:
The Corporate Services Manager plays a pivotal leadership role in planning, directing, and coordinating the corporate, administrative, and operational functions of Exaudy Care Pty Ltd. This position ensures the efficient, compliant, and sustainable delivery of NDIS-funded disability and community support services by providing strategic advice to the Directors on governance, financial management, workforce capability, risk, and business growth. Working closely with leadership, the role is critical to strengthening organisational systems, driving operational excellence, and supporting the company’s mission to deliver high-quality, participant-centred care.
Key Responsibilities:
Plan, organise, direct and coordinate the overall corporate and administrative operations of Exaudy Care Pty Ltd to ensure the efficient delivery of disability support, Supported Independent Living (SIL), Support Coordination, Behaviour Support and other community services.
Provide strategic, operational and administrative advice to the Directors on business performance, organisational planning, workforce capability, compliance, financial management, risk management and continuous improvement.
Develop, implement and review organisational policies, procedures, systems and operational frameworks to ensure compliance with the NDIS Practice Standards, NDIS Code of Conduct, Work Health and Safety legislation, Privacy legislation and other applicable Commonwealth and Victorian regulatory requirements.
Oversee all corporate services functions, including administration, human resources, compliance, information management, procurement, facilities management, fleet coordination, rostering support, information technology systems and general business operations.
Manage the organisation's administrative, financial, physical and human resources to maximise operational efficiency, service quality, regulatory compliance and sustainable organisational growth.
Coordinate annual business planning and budgeting processes, monitor operational expenditure, analyse financial performance and prepare management reports, forecasts and recommendations to support informed strategic decision-making.
Develop and maintain effective organisational governance systems, including document control, record management, quality assurance, internal audits, incident management oversight, risk registers, corrective actions and continuous improvement activities.
Monitor organisational performance through service delivery data, compliance reporting, financial analysis, workforce metrics and participant outcomes, identifying opportunities to improve operational efficiency, governance and business performance.
Lead and manage the organisation's administrative and corporate support workforce, including recruitment, onboarding, workforce planning, performance management, training, succession planning and professional development.
Coordinate recruitment and workforce planning processes to ensure appropriate staffing levels, skill mix and operational capability across disability services, administrative functions and corporate operations.
Oversee organisational procurement activities, supplier and contractor management, asset management and facilities coordination to support efficient business operations and high-quality service delivery.
Prepare, review and present business reports, operational analyses, policy documents, management submissions, funding reports and correspondence for Directors, government agencies, auditors, the NDIS Commission and other external stakeholders.
Establish and maintain productive relationships with participants, families, support coordinators, government departments, funding bodies, community organisations, allied health providers, suppliers, contractors and other strategic partners.
Represent Exaudy Care Pty Ltd in meetings, negotiations, industry forums, compliance reviews, quality audits, conferences and stakeholder consultations.
Support the Directors in implementing business expansion initiatives, new service development, organisational restructuring, digital transformation projects and continuous improvement strategies.
Analyse complex organisational, operational, compliance and resource management issues and provide evidence-based recommendations to improve governance, financial performance, operational effectiveness, participant outcomes and organisational growth.
Requirements:
Australian citizens and permanent residents are encouraged to apply.
Bachelor degree or higher qualifications (at least five years of relevant experience may substitute for the formal qualification).
At least 1 year of relevant experience is required.
Demonstrated experience in corporate services leadership, including finance, HR, operations, procurement, and facilities management.
Excellent analytical, organisational, and problem-solving skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a dynamic environment.
Superior interpersonal and communication skills, with proven ability to build relationships with stakeholders, lead teams, and represent the organisation professionally.
High level of integrity, attention to detail, and commitment to continuous improvement and regulatory compliance.
How to Apply:
To apply, applicants must submit their resume with a valid email address through this online portal.
Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

# Motor Mechanic

## About Gold Coast Car Electrics & Mechanical

Gold Coast Car Electrics & Mechanical is a trusted independent automotive workshop committed to delivering high-quality mechanical repairs, servicing and diagnostic solutions. We service a wide range of petrol, diesel and hybrid vehicles, combining advanced diagnostic technology with skilled workmanship to ensure our customers' vehicles remain safe, reliable and performing at their best.

We are seeking a qualified and motivated **Motor Mechanic** to join our growing team. This is an excellent opportunity for someone who takes pride in their workmanship, enjoys solving technical problems and values delivering outstanding customer service.

## Key Responsibilities

As a Motor Mechanic, you will be responsible for:

* Diagnosing mechanical faults using diagnostic equipment and technical expertise.
* Performing servicing, maintenance and repairs on petrol, diesel and hybrid vehicles in accordance with manufacturer specifications.
* Inspecting engines, transmissions, suspension, steering, braking and cooling systems to identify faults and determine repair requirements.
* Removing, dismantling, repairing and replacing worn or defective mechanical components.
* Carrying out engine tuning, timing adjustments and performance-related repairs to ensure optimum vehicle operation.
* Inspecting and repairing driveline components, clutches, gearboxes, differentials and exhaust systems.
* Completing scheduled logbook servicing, preventative maintenance and vehicle safety inspections.
* Testing vehicles before and after repairs to verify that faults have been rectified and the vehicle is safe and roadworthy.
* Maintaining accurate service records and clearly communicating repair recommendations to customers and the service team.
* Ensuring all work is completed efficiently while complying with workplace health and safety requirements and industry standards.
* Maintaining a clean, organised and safe workshop environment, including the proper care of tools and equipment.

## Essential Qualifications and Experience

* AQF Certificate III in Light Vehicle Mechanical Technology (or equivalent) with at least two years of on-the-job training, or AQF Certificate IV. Alternatively, a minimum of three years of relevant industry experience.
* At least two years' experience as a qualified Motor Mechanic is preferred.
* Current Australian driver's licence (preferred).

## Skills and Attributes

The successful applicant will demonstrate:

* Strong diagnostic and fault-finding skills across a wide range of vehicle makes and models.
* Sound knowledge of automotive mechanical systems and manufacturer repair procedures.
* Experience using modern diagnostic scan tools and workshop equipment.
* Excellent problem-solving and troubleshooting abilities.
* Strong customer service and communication skills.
* Good organisational and time-management skills with the ability to prioritise workloads.
* The ability to work independently and as part of a collaborative team.
* A strong commitment to quality workmanship, workplace safety and customer satisfaction.

## Employment Details

* **Position:** Permanent Full-Time
* **Salary:** AU$80,000 per annum plus employer superannuation contributions at the statutory rate.
* **Location:** Ashmore, Gold Coast, Queensland
* **Job Type:** Full-time

About CALHN
At Central Adelaide (CALHN), we're shaping the future of health through excellence in clinical care, research, and innovation. As South Australia's largest health network, we deliver exceptional, safe and connected healthcare - for our patients, our community, and our people.

With more than 17,000 dedicated employees, every day at CALHN presents an opportunity to make a real impact-not because it's expected, but because our values guide us to be our best. Find out more about CALHN sites and services, our stories and the opportunities to be part of CALHN.

About the Role

Join our Volunteer Services Unit and help keep things running smoothly behind the scenes. You'll manage day to day admin, build strong relationships with volunteers and staff, create accurate records and support meaningful services across Hampstead Rehabilitation Centre and the Repat Health Precinct. Every day brings variety and the chance to make a real difference. 

This role is required to work across both sites, providing flexible operational and administrative support wherever it is needed. Every day brings variety, the opportunity to work with a diverse range of people and services, and the chance to make a real difference to patients, volunteers and staff.

Key Responsibilities

Provide efficient admin support to the Volunteer Services Unit

About You

You're an organised and approachable administrator who enjoys supporting people and keeping things running smoothly. You thrive in a busy environment, communicate with confidence and take pride in delivering accurate, responsive and customer focused support.

- Experience in administration and customer service
- Skilled in Microsoft Word, Excel and Outlook
- Accurate data entry with strong attention to detail
- Balance priorities, protect confidentiality and meet deadlines
- Build positive relationships with diverse people and teams

Paid leave - with leave loading for rest and recharge
